title: Multimodal Hivemind: Do Vision-Language Models Describe Images Homogeneously?

original_idea.body:
# Multimodal Hivemind: Do Vision-Language Models Describe Images Homogeneously?

**Problem:** The Hivemind paper flags multimodal as an open extension. If VLMs give near-identical descriptions/judgments of ambiguous or safety-relevant images, they share visual blind spots.

**Direction:** Assemble ambiguous and safety-relevant images. Run ~6-8 open VLMs to produce descriptions and safety judgments. Measure inter-model homogeneity and agreement. Identify images where all VLMs share the same interpretation.

**Why it matters:** Shared visual blind spots matter for content moderation and physical-world deployments.

**Relevant context:** Artificial Hivemind multimodal extension hint (arXiv:2510.22954).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible (shared visual blind spots in moderation/perception) but the catastrophic link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Open VLMs plus embedding similarity; consumer GPU; curating safety images is modest extra work.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: VLM description/judgment homogeneity on a curated image set.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public VLMs, consumer GPU; multimodal extension the paper flags.

low_compute.reasoning: Small open VLMs on a single consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Explicit open multimodal extension; mostly unstudied but flagged.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Multimodal homogeneity flagged as open; largely unstudied.
